known_facts_book1: Queen of Oogaboo, a small valley kingdom in a far corner of the Land of Oz, over which she rules eighteen men, twenty-seven women and forty-four children.
Acts as Queen because her father King Jol Jemkiph Soforth crept over the pass and disappeared, and her mother went in search of him.
Sets out to conquer the world because she resents her tiny kingdom, after her sister Salye taunts her with the idea.
Raises an Army of exactly seventeen: sixteen officers — four Generals, four Colonels, four Majors and four Captains — and one Private, Files.
Wears an imposing green uniform covered with gold braid, with a green soldier-cap and a purple plume.
Never reaches the Land of Oz at all: Glinda reads of her plan in the Record Book and twists the mountain pass so the army emerges in an adjoining country instead.
Falls into Ruggedo's covered pit with all sixteen officers, escapes by touching a secret spring with her elbow, and crawls through a jagged tunnel that leads to the Metal Forest.
Emerges from the tunnel in rags, her crown bent and battered and her shoes cut to pieces.
Gives up conquering the world at the end and wishes only to be home; Ozma has the Wizard transport her and all her people back to Oogaboo.
Is allowed by King Kaliko to tie up a handkerchief full of diamonds before she leaves.

Taunts Ann by suggesting she raise an army and conquer Oz, which is what gives Ann the idea.

known_facts_book1: The eighteenth and last man of Oogaboo, an intelligent and ambitious young fellow who owns twelve trees bearing steel files and nine book-trees.

The books on his trees grow in green husks that turn deep red when ripe; picked too soon the stories are confused and the spelling bad, and once a book is read the words disappear and the leaves wither.
Insists on being sole Private rather than an officer, arguing from his story-books that it is always the private soldiers who do the fighting.
Picks his own musket from a gun-tree and his bullets from a bullet-tree.
Is the only one who faces the Rak: he loads his gun in the dark and shoots it, breaking its jaw, its left wing and its right leg.
Grows more cheerful the worse things get, which is what makes Ann consult him more often than her officers.
Resigns from the Army rather than obey the order to bind Betsy, Polychrome and Ozga, and throws down his gun and knapsack.
Suggests the Rose Princess ask the field-flowers the way, and they bend and nod three times toward Ruggedo's kingdom.
Becomes such a good friend of Ozga that Ozma sends her back to Oogaboo with him rather than separate them.

known_facts_book1: Sixteen men of Oogaboo, all named after the crop their orchard bears: Generals Apple, Bunn, Cone and Clock; Colonels Plum, Egg, Banjo and Cheese; Majors Nails, Cake, Ham and Stockings; Captains Sandwich, Padlocks, Sundae and Buttons.
Wear gorgeous uniforms and carry sharp glittering swords, but every one of them refuses to fight, saying they are brave in every way until it comes to fighting.
Each carries a tiny white tent in his pocket that grows to full size when placed on the ground.
Flee shrieking from the Rak, and afterwards argue that by running away they preserved themselves to assist the Queen.
Are routed twice by Hank's heels alone, dropping their swords and hiding behind trees and bushes.
March straight into Ruggedo's covered pit and are imprisoned there, then crawl for days through a jagged tunnel that rubs the skin off their knees and reduces their uniforms to rags.
Capture Ruggedo in the Metal Forest — their one act of courage in the whole book — not knowing he has already been deposed.
Are sent home to Oogaboo by the Wizard's magic at Ozma's command, every one of them longing for his orchard.
